title: Gross Body Composition Measurement Using DEXA
author: Trina Knotts
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.68ahhse
materials: Weigh animal on analytical scale and record measurement.

steps.title: Prepare DEXA Equipment
steps.instruction: Set up and calibrate the Piximus system prior to scanning.

substeps.instruction: Turn on Piximus at least 2 hours before the first scan.
Open Piximus software and initiate calibration using a 'phantom' (object with defined bone mineral density and fat content); this process takes approximately 1 hour.

steps.title: Prepare Animal for Scanning
steps.instruction: Anesthetize and measure the animal to ensure proper data recording.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize animal via inhalation using 2-4% isoflurane in O2.
Monitor anesthesia depth via toe and tail pinch; lack of response indicates adequate anesthesia.
Weigh animal on an analytical scale and record the measurement.

Measure animal length from the tip of the nose to the beginning of the tail (anus) to the nearest 0.5 cm using calipers, ensuring the spine is fully extended with a gentle pull, and record the measurement.

steps.title: Position Animal on Analyzer
steps.instruction: Place the unconscious mouse on the DEXA analyzer specimen tray with precise positioning.

substeps.instruction: Position the mouse with legs slightly outstretched and soles of feet down as much as possible.
Ensure the spine is in a straight line and the entire mouse is within the sticky pad outlines.
Position the nose within the nosecone (head to the left when looking at the machine).
Ensure the mouse is as flat as possible with the spine fully extended.
Handle the tail by either curling it around the left side toward the head (to include in analysis) or leaving it straight (to exclude from analysis).

steps.title: Execute DEXA Scan
steps.instruction: Enter subject data and perform the scan, verifying image alignment.

substeps.instruction: Enter subject ID, body weight, gender, date of birth, and body length measurements.
Start the scan.
Verify the first image on the screen; ensure all limbs and body are properly in the field. If incorrect, stop the run, reposition the mouse, and restart.
Allow the full scan to run (approximately 4-5 minutes).

steps.title: Post-Scan Animal Care
steps.instruction: Ensure the animal recovers safely after the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Return the mouse to its home cage.
Monitor recovery for 1 hour.

steps.title: Process Images and Calculate Data
steps.instruction: Process image files in Piximus software to refine analysis and calculate body composition.

substeps.instruction: Exclude the head region by adjusting the placement of the green circle in the software and reprocess the scan data.
Generate Bone area measurement by outlining skeletal bone regions (limbs, neck, spine, and tail) as regions of interest (ROI), excluding the head.
Generate Bone mineral content (BMC) using density scans assessed against hydroxyapatite standards (0.0 mg to 2,000 mg).
Calculate Bone Mineral Density (BMD) using the formula: BMD = BMC ÷ bone area.
Calculate Total body tissue weight: Total body tissue weight = (BMC + Body fat tissue weight + Lean body tissue weight).
Calculate Lean body (non-fat) tissue weight: Lean body tissue weight = (Total body tissue weight – body fat weight).
Calculate Body fat tissue weight: Body fat tissue weight = (Total body tissue weight - lean body tissue weight).
